assessments.reasoning: The introduction first describes PowerBuilder as an application-development product and then identifies PowerScript as the language in its event and function scripts. Its use of the names assigns different referents within one exact edition.

challenge.method: Compare the introduction’s product, script, and language passages with both original publisher covers, the same-numbered base 2022 cover, and the separately versioned Bridge API control.
challenge.results: The Getting Started and PowerScript Reference covers independently label the publication set Windows 2022 R3 and show the August 13, 2026 revision. The base 2022 reference reuses the PowerScript Reference document number and prints a different edition and November 24, 2022 revision. The Bridge page describes a distinct API version and bundle. The claimant’s limited language/product identity is supported by the exact R3 introduction.

limitations: The paired covers authenticate the edition of the cited publications. No separate numbered language release, backward compatibility, or product-to-language classifier equivalence is inferred.
